title: AlpaServe: Statistical Multiplexing with Model Parallelism for Deep Learning Serving
technique: simulator-guided model placement and cluster group partition combining inter-/intra-op model parallelism across multiple models to statistically multiplex GPUs under bursty traffic

optimized_metrics.evidence: it then partitions and places the models and schedules the requests to optimize SLO attainment (i.e., the percentage of requests served within SLO).
Our goal is to find a placement that maximizes the SLO attainment.

headline_claim.text: AlpaServe can process requests at up to 10x higher rates or 6x more burstiness while staying within latency constraints for more than 99% of requests.

reported_metrics.where: Figs 12-15 (vs rate, CV, SLO scale, #devices); 99% goal
Figs 2-5 motivation (mean and P99 latency, CDF)
max sustainable request rate at 99% attainment; Fig 9b
minimal number of devices needed at 99% attainment

metric_definitions.definition_quote: SLO attainment (i.e., the percentage of requests served within SLO)
metric_definitions.notes: request considered served if it finishes within deadline, where latency 'includes the GPU execution time and queuing delay' (§3.1)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: request latency (which includes the GPU execution time and queuing delay)
metric_definitions.notes: whole-request latency; models are single-pass (BERT, MoE) with fixed execution time

metric_definitions.definition_quote: the default SLO is set as tight as 5x inference latency (SLO Scale=5)
metric_definitions.notes: SLO = SLO-scale multiple of single-device inference latency

metric_definitions.definition_quote: We use SLO attainment as the major evaluation metric. Under a specific SLO attainment goal (say, 99%), we concern with another four measures: (1) the minimal number of devices the system needs, (2) the maximum average request rate, (3) the maximum traffic burstiness the system can support, and (4) the minimal SLO the system can handle.
metric_definitions.notes: optimizes one of four capacity measures at a time at a fixed 99% attainment

slo_spec: SLO = SLO Scale x single-device inference latency (default scale 5); attainment goal 99%; scale swept; following Clockwork and InferLine
load_regime: trace replay (Azure MAF1, MAF2) with swept rate scale, burstiness (CV), SLO scale and #devices; Gamma processes for synthetic
tradeoff_acknowledged: model parallelism adds overhead (communication, stage imbalance) vs statistical multiplexing benefit; with loose SLO or high rate, replication outperforms model parallelism ('model parallelism is beneficial for smaller SLOs')
hardware: 64 GPUs: 8 nodes x 8 NVIDIA Tesla V100-16GB; simulator validated (<2% error)
models: BERT-1.3B/2.7B/6.7B/104B, GShard MoE (non-autoregressive; extension to GPT-3-style generation only discussed)
workloads: Azure Function traces MAF1 (2019) and MAF2 (2021) mapped to models
extractor_notes: Not autoregressive LLM generation: models are single-forward-pass with deterministic latency, so no TTFT/TBT. Still a DL/LLM-adjacent serving system and used as a baseline in later LLM work; kept in scope. Motivation uses mean and P99 latency; the system objective is attainment.
load_class_quote: trace replay (Azure MAF1, MAF2) with swept rate scale, burstiness (CV) and SLO scale; Gamma processes for synthetic traffic (§6.1)
